Subject: SIG follow-up — hosting mode evidence and network boundaries

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for sending the initial SIG answers last week. Our security team had a couple of follow-up asks specifically around how Redwood defines and evidences the different hosting modes (Hosted, Dedicated, Private/VPC/on-prem). They would like: 

- A short, plain-English summary of key responsibilities (who manages data at rest, who manages keys, who patches the runtime) for each mode.
- A network boundary diagram that shows where customer traffic enters, what stays in Redwood control plane, and where customer-managed infrastructure sits for Private mode.
- Confirmation on whether Dedicated uses the same control plane as Hosted (and if so, what isolation guarantees exist).
- A link to any audit evidence (SOC 2 section pointers) or a specific place in the SIG spreadsheet where we state the controls.

Can you provide a consolidated response and evidence so our CISO can close their review tomorrow? Attaching the remaining questionnaire sections would be helpful.

Best,
Ashley

Hi Ashley,

Thanks — appreciate the clear asks. I attached a focused pack (SIG_Answers_v3.xlsx) and an updated network diagram (network_topology_v2.pdf). High-level answers below; the spreadsheet has row-level cross-references to SOC 2 sections and our public compliance page.

Quick summary (plain-English):
- Hosted (Redwood Hosted API): Redwood manages the full runtime, underlying GPUs, and the control plane. Customer data is encrypted at rest and in transit; encryption keys are managed by Redwood (KMS) by default. Customers may request additional contractual protections and dedicated ingestion endpoints. See spreadsheet: sheet "Hosted" rows A10-A25.
- Dedicated (Reserved capacity): Compute nodes are dedicated to the customer but the control plane (orchestration, billing, routing) remains in Redwood's control plane. Isolation is achieved at the GPU/VM level with tenant-only scheduling and network-level segmentation. Data access controls and audit logs are scoped per-tenant. See sheet "Dedicated" rows B5-B30.
- Private / VPC / On-prem: Customer runs inference in a customer-managed VPC or on-prem cluster. Control plane can be configured as customer-controlled (private control plane) or as a thin, customer-approved connector to Redwood's management plane. Customers retain responsibility for patching the host environment and key management when opting for customer-managed KMS. See sheet "Private" rows C8-C40.

Isolation and control plane note: Dedicated uses Redwood's hosted control plane by default. We provide strict tenant isolation primitives (no cross-tenant KV access, per-tenant audit logs, network ACLs) and can add a dedicated control plane in enterprise engagements where contractually required — we document this in the spreadsheet and in the deployment map image.

Attachments included: 1) SIG_Answers_v3.xlsx — a condensed SIG answer set with explicit evidence links and SOC 2 crosswalk; 2) network_topology_v2.pdf — annotated boundary diagram; 3) redwood_deployment_map.png — simplified mode comparison.

Next steps:
- If you want KMS details or an HSM addendum for Private mode, I can loop in Legal (Laura Bennett).
- If your network team wants the diagram in Visio, Jonas can provide the editable source.

I've looped in internal leads for a quick Q&A below.

Thanks,
Soojin

Hi Ashley,

Following up with the consolidated pack and a couple clarifications from our security and legal teams. See attachments — I've updated the spreadsheet per Jonas' notes and added the Private/KMS callout in the network diagram. Key highlights below (short):

- Hosted: Redwood-managed runtime and keys by default; SOC 2 controls mapped in SIG_Answers_v3.xlsx (sheet "Hosted", ref S2-3).
- Dedicated: Tenant-dedicated compute; hosted control plane by default but isolated via tenant scheduling, ACLs, and per-tenant audit logs. We state this explicitly in B12-B14 of the spreadsheet. Dedicated can be paired with a contractually-dedicated control plane in enterprise deals.
- Private/VPC/On-prem: Customer is responsible for host patching and may bring their own KMS/HSM. When customer-managed KMS is configured, key material does not transit Redwood-managed systems — callout added to network_topology_v2.pdf.

Evidence pointers: 
- SIG_Answers_v3.xlsx includes SOC 2 crosswalk (sheet "Evidence") and links to our public compliance page.
- Network diagram attached demonstrates ingress points and optional private control plane configurations.

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute call with Jonas and Laura tomorrow morning to walk through the diagram and the SOC 2 crosswalk. Does 9:30 AM PT work for your team?

Thanks — I know your timeline is tight; happy to iterate.

Best,
Soojin
